skill.name: lint-and-validate
skill.description: Run project linting, type checks, and static validation after code changes using common Node.js and Python tooling.
skill.summary: Runs lint, type, and security validation workflows for Node.js and Python projects.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The Python runner genuinely executes lint commands in the target project, including project-defined npm lint scripts. Several SKILL.md command examples are actionable because the skill allows Bash, while pure command-name and filename mentions are false positives. No prompt injection or explicit data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Project-defined lint scripts can execute arbitrary commands.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit user approval before running npm scripts or npx commands, and show the command and working directory first.

remediation.issue: The runner accepts any project path from the command line.
remediation.suggestion: Constrain execution to the current workspace, or require confirmation before running tools outside the active repository.

remediation.issue: Validation guidance treats command execution as mandatory.
remediation.suggestion: Document that validation commands should be skipped or confirmed when the repository is untrusted.

static_findings.snippet: - If `lint` fails: Fix the style or syntax issues immediately.
- If `tsc` fails: Correct type mismatches before proceeding.
- If no tool is configured: Check the project root for `.eslintrc`, `tsconfig.json`, `pyproject.toml

finding_verdicts.reason: subprocess.run executes linter command arrays inside the selected project directory. The npm lint path can invoke project-controlled package scripts, so untrusted repositories can execute local commands.
The line instructs the agent to run npm lint or npx eslint with Bash access. npm run lint executes project-defined scripts, which is risky in untrusted repositories.
The line instructs the agent to run npx tsc, which executes a project tool from the local environment. This is expected validation behavior but still external command execution.
The line instructs the agent to run npm audit. This invokes an external package manager command and may disclose dependency metadata to the configured npm registry.
The line instructs the agent to run ruff with fix mode over a path. It is legitimate linting guidance, but it executes an installed binary and can modify files.
The line instructs the agent to run Bandit recursively over a path. This is normal security scanning, but it is still external command execution on repository contents.
The line instructs the agent to run mypy on a path. This is legitimate type checking, but it executes an installed external tool in the project context.
The quality loop instructs npm run lint followed by npx tsc. The npm script component can execute arbitrary commands from package.json in an untrusted project.
This line only mentions the word lint in Markdown error-handling text. It does not introduce a command invocation or shell execution instruction.
This line only names tsc in Markdown prose about failures. It does not instruct a new command execution or expose a shell primitive.
The backticks wrap configuration filenames in documentation. File names such as tsconfig.json and pyproject.toml are not executable commands.
The line documents running the bundled lint runner with a project path. That runner executes external lint commands, including project-defined npm scripts.
The line documents running the bundled type coverage script, which reads source files and reports coverage. I did not find evidence that this script executes project code.

content.value_statement: Code changes often fail because lint, type, or audit checks are skipped. This skill guides agents through repeatable validation for Node.js and Python projects.
actual_capabilities: Identifies Node.js and Python validation workflows from common project files.
Runs configured lint checks for npm, ESLint, Ruff, and related tools.
Runs TypeScript and Python type checks when project configuration exists.
Summarizes pass and fail results after validation commands complete.
Includes a type coverage helper for TypeScript and Python source files.
limitations: It depends on tools already installed in the local environment.
It may run project-defined npm scripts, so untrusted repositories need caution.
It does not replace a full test suite or manual security review.
Type coverage checks use simple pattern matching and can miss complex cases.

use_cases.title: Pre-commit Validation
use_cases.description: Run lint and type checks before reporting a code change as complete.

use_cases.title: Agent Quality Gate
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code a consistent checklist after edits.

use_cases.title: Repository Health Review
use_cases.description: Check whether a project has common validation tools configured and usable.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Validation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request after a small edit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the current project after my changes. Run the appropriate lint and type checks, then summarize any failures.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Lint Failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request when lint output is expected.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the project lint workflow. Fix clear style or syntax issues, then rerun validation until the lint check passes or needs my decision.

prompt_templates.title: Check Types and Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Run lint, type checks, and configured security audit commands for this repository. Report each result and the remaining risk.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Validation Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for maintainers improving project standards.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the repository validation setup. Identify missing lint, type, or audit configuration, then propose the smallest practical improvements.

output_examples.input: Validate a TypeScript project after a component update.
output: Lint passed with no remaining style errors.
Type checking failed in one component because a required prop was missing.
Recommended next step: update the prop usage and rerun validation.

output_examples.input: Review a Python project before marking a bug fix complete.
output: Ruff found formatting issues and corrected them.
Mypy reported two missing annotations in changed functions.
Recommended next step: add the annotations and repeat the check.

output_examples.input: Check whether a repository has validation tools configured.
output_examples.output: The project has lint and type checks configured, but no security audit command was detected. Add one before release validation.

best_practices: Run validation from the repository root so tools find their configuration files.
Review commands before running them in repositories from unknown sources.
Rerun failed checks after fixes and report the final result clearly.
anti_patterns: Do not run project-defined scripts from untrusted repositories without user approval.
Do not treat passing lint as proof that the code is correct or secure.
Do not ignore missing tool configuration when a project should enforce standards.

faq.question: What tools does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses common Node.js and Python validation tools such as npm lint, ESLint, TypeScript, Ruff, Bandit, and Mypy.

faq.question: Does it fix code automatically?
faq.answer: It can use tool fix modes when the workflow requests them, but complex failures still need code changes.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Some validation commands can run project-defined scripts, so review commands before execution.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on lint, type, audit, and type coverage workflows, not application test suites.

faq.question: Can Claude Code and Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What happens when no linter is configured?
faq.answer: The skill asks the agent to check common configuration files and suggest adding a validation setup.
